headline: Test 2: Virginia, 1640–1705 · 42:33

items.title: 42:33 · Our second historical test moves from fifteenth-century
items.detail: Our second historical test moves from fifteenth-century Lisbon to seventeenth-century Virginia between 1619 and 1705, drawn from Chapter 4 of The Original Power.

items.title: 42:42 · This case tests Prediction 2 Codification follows
items.detail: This case tests Prediction 2, Codification follows solidarity threats: the prediction that rigid statutory race codes and Buffer Class privileges are enacted in direct response to cross-racial labor coalitions.

items.title: 42:54 · The Virginia record opens in late August
items.detail: The Virginia record opens in late August 1619 at Point Comfort, when the privateer vessel White Lion traded twenty and odd Angolan captives seized from the Portuguese slave ship Sao Joao Bautista.

items.title: 43:07 · For the first several decades of the
items.detail: For the first several decades of the Chesapeake tobacco economy, English statute law contained zero comprehensive slave codes and zero statutory definition of a white racial tier.

items.title: 43:18 · On the tobacco plantations of early Virginia
items.detail: On the tobacco plantations of early Virginia and Maryland, African laborers worked, ate, slept, and ran away alongside a massive population of European indentured servants.
